ov: An all-white whale of the Arctic and sub-Arctic, the narwhal’s closest relative. It has no dorsal fin, which helps it swim under ice, and a very bulbous melon on its forehead for echolocation, which also helps it find breathing holes in sea ice.

why.et: Indigenous hunters in Canada, Greenland, Alaska and Russia are allowed to hunt belugas for food.

df: Mainly fish, such as Arctic cod, salmon, herring, capelin and halibut, plus shrimp; it varies with place and season.

cf.tip: The beluga and narwhal are close relatives; only the narwhal has a tusk.

fx: Its melon is so bulbous and lobed that its head shape is unlike any other whale’s.
The most abundant toothed whale in the Arctic, it can dive to 700 m.
